topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening introduces the scope of the lecture on cancer therapy and outlines its core learning objectives.

topics.label: Conventional modalities, cytotoxic chemotherapy, and drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional local and systemic interventions—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutics—along with their systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting cellular vulnerabilities, checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapeutic approaches that exploit intrinsic cancer cell weaknesses, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinases and overcoming inhibitor resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the inhibition of aberrant kinase drivers and the molecular mechanisms underlying resistance and addiction to kinase-targeted therapies.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the design and therapeutic applications of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-cytotoxin conjugates targeting surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and immune-cell engagement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and examine immunotherapies including checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Therapeutic challenges, historical progress, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader clinical challenges, long-term mortality trends, ethical dilemmas, and emerging strategies shaping the future of cancer management.
